planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; Kit Cat is a true dwarf selection bred for a tight, non-sprawling mound noticeably smaller than 'Walker's Low' or 'Six Hills Giant'.

directions: Kit Cat forms a dense, tidy dome of small, gray-green, scalloped foliage covered in lavender-blue flower spikes from late spring into early fall, holding its rounded shape without the sprawl typical of larger faassenii cultivars. Its compact size makes it well suited to the front of a border, rock garden, or container planting where taller catmints would flop or overwhelm neighbors. Shear back by about a third after the first flush of bloom to keep the mound neat and to encourage steady rebloom through summer. Once established it is highly drought-tolerant, needs no staking, and draws bees continuously through its long flowering season.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Kitten Around is a patented, compact Proven Winners introduction bred for an especially tight, round habit and an early, extended bloom flush.

directions: Kitten Around builds a tight, rounded mound of aromatic gray-green leaves set off by rosy-purple calyxes that hold periwinkle-blue flowers in a nearly continuous flush from late spring well into summer. Its uniform, non-flopping habit suits edging, containers, and small-space borders where larger catmints need frequent staking or shearing to look tidy. Cut plants back by roughly a third after the first heavy bloom period to refresh the foliage and prompt a second round of flowers. It tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil once established, and its long nectar season makes it a reliable draw for bees.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Souvenir d'André Chaudron Siberian Catmint (Giant Catmint)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this 1948 Frank Skinner introduction is a taller, more cold-hardy Siberian species selection and an RHS Award of Garden Merit holder, distinct from the more commonly grown Nepeta x faassenii cultivars.

directions: This slowly suckering Siberian catmint sends up sturdy, upright stems clothed in aromatic, lance-shaped deep green leaves, topped from early summer into fall with loose spikes of unusually large lavender-blue flowers held well above the foliage. Its taller, more upright habit and outstanding cold hardiness set it apart from the lower, sprawling Nepeta x faassenii hybrids, and it tolerates somewhat more moisture in the soil without declining. Plants spread gently by rhizomes to form a broadening clump rather than self-sowing, so division every few years both controls spread and renews vigor. Butterflies and bees visit steadily through its long season, while deer and rabbits generally leave it untouched.
